slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every number a. Diamond of a is equal to a squared minus four a. Diamond of six is equal to what?

slides: So we have a rule, and we need to use it on the number six. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, first by putting six straight into the rule, and then by simplifying the rule before we use it.

slides.say: [short pause] Remember what the rule means. Whatever goes into the diamond takes the place of a, in every spot where a appears. Here a appears in two spots, in a squared and in four a. So we write the same template again, and put six in both spots.
So diamond of six is six squared minus four times six. Six squared is thirty-six. Four times six is twenty-four. Thirty-six minus twenty-four is twelve.
So diamond of six is twelve, and choice number two is our answer. Careful, thirty-six, choice number one, is what you get if you put six only into a squared and forget the four a.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to simplify the rule first, and only then put the number in. Both parts of a squared minus four a have an a in them: a squared is a times a, and four a is a times four. So we can write the whole expression as a times something. a squared minus four a is a times, in brackets, a minus four. Let's check it. a times a is a squared, and a times negative four is negative four a.
at: a squared minus four a is a times

slides.say: Now put six in. Six times, in brackets, six minus four. Six minus four is two, and six times two is twelve. Again twelve, choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
